A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MuSe research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching retained derivations across the substantial revision.

before.justification: V1 reports original attention microbenchmarks, component ablations and approximately 30M-parameter model pretraining on PG-19, including additional appendix experiments.

after.justification: V3 reports original microbenchmarks, multi-scale pretraining, MoBA comparisons, pretrained-Llama evaluations, downstream results and fine-tuning experiments.

M1.justification: V3 replaces dipole corrections in the main method with two-level selection of key clusters and spatial blocks for exact retrieval. Causal accumulation of block summaries replaces v1's binary-tree decomposition, and streaming K-means replaces the earlier iterative clustering procedure. Separate query/key clustering and exponential tilting remain; dipoles survive as an appendix alternative.

E1.justification: Pretraining coverage changes from PG-19 books to Python repositories from The Stack v2 and scientific documents from OLMo 3 LongMino. PG-19 remains in pretrained-Llama evaluation, while ARC-Easy and SciQ add downstream task coverage (v3 Appendix G.2).

E2.justification: CUDNN and Pallas exact attention remain runtime comparators. V3 adds MoBA comparisons at matched far-field sparsity in microbenchmarks and pretraining (Tables 1 and 6), plus an alternative MoBA compute allocation in Table 21. V1 contains no evaluated competing sparse-attention method.

E3.justification: V1's 29.4M-parameter, 16k-context, 2B-token pretraining setup with one global attention layer is replaced by 96M–1B models at 64k context, alternating local/global layers and budgets up to 23.6B tokens. V3 also introduces matched-sparsity controls, cross-evaluation with exact attention, head-dimension-128 tests, a 100-chunk Llama evaluation and downstream accuracy metrics.

E4.justification: V1's early/late component ablations and cluster-cap/iteration sweeps are substantially reworked. V3 separates query-clustering benefits for summaries versus retrieval, varies retrieval budgets and spatial blocks, and studies scaling with context. New analyses test exponential tilting on Llama, context utilization during training and exact-attention fine-tuning to remove adaptation (Appendices B and E–G).

E5.justification: V3 adds approximate standard-error reporting for downstream results (Table 25), fixed-seed clustering initialization disclosure, and power-law estimation with explicitly marked extrapolations (Table 2). V1 lacks these practices. Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty for its headline pretraining comparisons.

E6.justification: V1 Table 4 reports PG-19 losses of 3.310 for Pallas and 3.322 for MuSe. V3 Table 4 instead reports new 1B code results: 0.7026 for the CUDNN baseline, 0.7001 for MuSe evaluated with MuSe, and 0.7108 when evaluated with CUDNN before fine-tuning. Numerous MoBA, scaling, ablation and downstream outcomes are added. Different methods and settings preclude direct cross-version performance comparisons.

T1.justification: V1's binary-tree derivation of O(NCD log N) causal complexity is removed. V3 formalizes block-indexed summaries and retrieval scores and instead discusses fixed sparsity, explicitly retaining quadratic local-attention cost at fixed block count (Appendix F.5). The cumulant expansions and dipole error orders remain in Appendix B; their relocation itself does not constitute new theory.

C1.justification: V1 emphasizes the viability of dipole-based pretraining with small loss degradation and linear/log-linear complexity. V3 centers its contribution on retrieval-augmented attention, baseline-quality 1B/64k pretraining, 36% throughput improvement and 64-fold far-field sparsity, with explicit claims about pretrained-model compatibility and preserved context utilization.

C2.justification: V3 explains retrieval as handling sharp attention while summaries approximate smooth contributions. It adds interpretations involving implicit regularization, adaptation to approximate attention, catastrophic failure without tilting on Llama, and fine-tuning as a remedy for interchangeability loss. It also discusses dipole/retrieval incompatibilities, distributed extensions and remaining local-attention costs.

D1.justification: V3 substantially expands v1 Appendix A's reproducibility information. Appendices C–D document streaming-clustering updates, initialization, precision, centroid-gradient handling, dataset filtering and concatenation, per-scale hyperparameters, eight-A100 hardware and sharding. The method section additionally explains segmented retrieval and index arrays. Newly documented choices do not independently establish changes to previously undisclosed implementation behavior.

R1.justification: Positioning shifts from novelty through higher-order dipoles toward query-specific summaries and retrieval compared with MoBA's spatial sparsity and inference-only key clustering. V3 adds MoBA, FlashMoBA, FlashInfer and scaling/data references, while removing the A2ATS, Perceiver and Luna discussions and citations.

P1.justification: The abstract and contributions are rewritten, related work is compressed, and v1's separate monopole, dipole, algorithm and causal sections become one pipeline-focused method section. Dipole mathematics moves to Appendix B, and the experimental narrative is reorganized around scaling, pretraining and generalization. This constitutes extensive rewriting beyond adding results.

P2.justification: V3 replaces the binary-tree diagram with a detailed retrieval/accumulation overview, redraws the geometric illustration and adds scaling, Llama and position-loss plots. Component pseudocode is consolidated into one causal algorithm. Tables are extensively reorganized, training plots use wall-clock time, and the document switches to a two-column layout.

improvement.justification: V3 substantially addresses v1's limited validation through multi-scale, two-domain pretraining, a competing sparse-attention baseline, pretrained-model compatibility tests and detailed mechanism analyses. These provide stronger evidence for practical usefulness and clarify adaptation risks. The 1B code result needs additional exact-attention fine-tuning for full interchangeability, and uncertainty for small loss advantages remains limited, but the broader controlled evidence and expanded reproducibility information substantially improve the paper.
